archive.omitted: Earlier snapshots, bulk volume/hash inventories, operational recovery scripts, and PR drafts remain available at this exact commit.

official_protocol.dataset_scope: 24 configured float datasets: 19 current and 5 deprecated; int8, uint8, binary, and chamfer datasets require unsupported HMS interfaces
official_protocol.splits: Official HDF5 train corpus, test queries and truth; OOD learn queries supplied to fit_ood without access to learn neighbors by HMS
official_protocol.preprocessing: Official VIBE HDF5 data and loader; normalized datasets use VIBE-normalized float32 rows
official_protocol.metrics: VIBE recall@100 (distance tolerance 0.001), best QPS of five full query passes, build time, index size
official_protocol.operation_sequence: download and verify dataset; build each index; search all test queries for each query configuration five times; export summary
official_protocol.timing_boundaries: VIBE runner times algo.query for each CPU query with time.perf_counter, excludes post-query truth-distance calculation, and retains best QPS of five passes
official_protocol.threads: one pinned worker core per index; math-library thread variables set to 1
official_protocol.official_hardware: Intel Xeon Gold 6230 with AVX-512, one core per algorithm, at least 16 GiB per used core recommended
official_protocol.official_limits: 24-hour timeout per individual algorithm run; no published fixed memory cap
official_protocol.modal_hardware: Per-container CPU model, AVX-512, allocated memory, and process state are in the ledger and cpu records; VIBE falls back from unavailable numactl to taskset pinning; HMS and competitors are scheduled in one dataset job, with possible container handovers
official_protocol.modal_memory_note: Several small-dataset Modal requests are below VIBE's recommendation of 16 GiB per used core; Modal memory requests are soft minimums, with actual usage allowed to burst. These rows are not an exact published-hardware reproduction
official_protocol.comparability: Cross-hardware published Xeon QPS is diagnostic only; use same-container HMS/competitor measurements when they complete, and verify CPU identity after any handover

verification_scope: Committed Parquet rows support offline reproduction of threshold standings. Receipts preserve original native/truth hashes; raw predictions, timings and truth arrays are external historical artifacts, so native recall cannot be independently recomputed from this directory alone.
native_build_receipt_coverage: 19 active-container wheel/module hashes captured after measurement began, plus Arxiv pre-index hashes; finished-container install logs retained without inventing binary hashes

curation.maintained_runner_note: Historical provenance, memory matching, native receipt and billing fixes retained; the existing run namespace and 64-GiB planning cap are preserved. Current source is not represented as the historical uploaded runner.
